hero.description: The US-Iran conflict has entered a more dangerous phase, with attacks involving oil tankers, military targets and commercial shipping pushing Brent crude above $100 a barrel and threatening another global inflation shock.

featured.title: Shipping Crisis Deepens as Oil Breaks Above $100
featured.content: The Middle East conflict has intensified sharply, with Iran saying it attacked 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz after the United States destroyed five Iranian oil tankers. At least one seafarer has reportedly been killed and another is missing. Preliminary Kpler data showed only six commodity vessels crossed the Strait on Tuesday, compared with a 10-day average of about 12. Brent crude subsequently moved above $100 a barrel, increasing fears that prolonged disruption could push up fuel, transport and food costs around the world.

articles.title: Iran Says It Attacked 10 Ships Near Strait of Hormuz
articles.content: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it attacked 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz after the United States destroyed five Iranian oil tankers. Iran also fired missiles towards a U.S.-used military base in Jordan. The United States says the attacks on its naval vessels failed, while the maritime confrontation has sharply increased risks to commercial shipping.
articles.imageQuery: Strait of Hormuz commercial ships oil tankers

articles.title: At Least One Seafarer Reportedly Killed in Latest Maritime Attacks
articles.content: At least one sailor has been reported killed and another remains missing following the latest attacks involving vessels around the Strait of Hormuz. Iran and the United States have issued conflicting accounts of the maritime confrontation, making independent verification of individual incidents difficult.

articles.title: Hormuz Shipping Falls to Six Commodity Vessels
articles.content: Preliminary shipping data shows only six commodity vessels passed through the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, down from nine the previous day and below the 10-day average of about 12. The figures may change because some vessels switch off their tracking transponders during voyages.
articles.imageQuery: Strait of Hormuz cargo ships aerial

articles.title: Brent Crude Breaks Above $100
articles.content: Brent crude moved above $100 a barrel on Wednesday for the first time since July as the latest escalation raised fears of prolonged disruption to Middle East oil flows. Reuters reported Brent at around $101.32 and U.S. West Texas Intermediate at about $96.48 during the latest trading session.
articles.imageQuery: Brent crude oil price oil barrels

articles.title: Houthi Attacks Add Pressure to Saudi Energy Security
articles.content: Iran-aligned Houthi forces have launched attacks against several locations in Saudi Arabia, including energy-related targets. The developments are raising concerns about both Gulf shipping and the Red Sea route, which is an important alternative pathway for energy transportation.
articles.imageQuery: Saudi Arabia oil facility energy infrastructure

articles.title: Dangote Plans $15–16bn Refinery in Kenya
articles.content: Aliko Dangote is planning a proposed $15–16bn refinery in Lamu, Kenya, with a planned capacity of 700,000 barrels per day. Groundbreaking is expected later this month and completion is targeted around 2030. The project faces major challenges, particularly securing reliable crude supplies, financing and infrastructure. Kenya currently has no commercial crude production.
articles.imageQuery: Lamu Kenya coast refinery industrial project

articles.title: Dangote Expands Energy Ambitions Beyond Nigeria
articles.content: The proposed Kenyan refinery forms part of Dangote's broader strategy to expand its energy business across Africa. The company is simultaneously pursuing a major expansion of its Nigerian refinery, which currently operates at around 700,000 barrels per day.

articles.title: Nigeria Kidnapping Victims' Families Still Await Answers
articles.content: Weeks after gunmen attacked communities in Niger State, families say they have received little information about relatives who were kidnapped. Reuters reported that the August 22 attack on Dekera and nearby communities killed dozens and resulted in hundreds of people being abducted. Families continue to demand information and stronger government action.
articles.imageQuery: Nigeria Niger State village security kidnapping

articles.title: Nigeria Security Crisis Highlights Need for Faster Response
articles.content: The continuing uncertainty surrounding the Dekera mass abduction has renewed concerns over intelligence gathering, early warning systems and rapid-response capacity in vulnerable communities. Residents say insecurity has already affected schools, markets and normal economic activity.

articles.title: Iraq Faces Resistance Over Militia Disarmament Plan
articles.content: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi is facing resistance from powerful Iran-backed Shi'ite militia groups over a government plan to bring weapons under state control by September 30. The deadline coincides with the planned withdrawal of remaining U.S.-led coalition forces from Iraq. Several influential militia groups have rejected the disarmament timetable.

articles.title: UK Air-Traffic Failure Disrupts More Than 2,000 Flights
articles.content: A major technical failure in the UK's air-traffic control system operated by NATS caused widespread disruption across British airports. More than 2,000 flights were cancelled and hundreds of thousands of passengers were affected. Although the technical problem was resolved, airlines continued dealing with aircraft and crew disruptions on Wednesday. The UK government has ordered an investigation into the incident.
articles.imageQuery: Heathrow airport passengers flight delays UK

articles.title: Europe's Energy Security Faces Renewed Pressure
articles.content: The European Court of Auditors says the EU's efforts to end dependence on Russian energy are faltering as the bloc faces renewed pressure from the Middle East conflict. EU gas storage facilities were around 67% full, below the roughly 80% level recorded at the same point last year. The auditors warned that insufficient investment in renewable energy, grids and energy diversification remains a concern.

articles.title: Global Markets Brace for Higher Energy Costs
articles.content: Investors remain cautious as oil prices move above $100 and geopolitical risks increase. Higher energy costs could feed into inflation, transportation expenses and business operating costs while making monetary-policy decisions more difficult for central banks.
articles.imageQuery: global financial markets trading screens oil

articles.title: Infrastructure Resilience Back in Focus After UK Aviation Failure
articles.content: The UK air-traffic control disruption has renewed scrutiny of the resilience of critical digital infrastructure. The incident highlights how a technical systems failure can rapidly affect airlines, airports, businesses and hundreds of thousands of travellers.

articles.title: Asian Markets Watch Oil and Geopolitical Risks
articles.content: Asian investors are closely monitoring the impact of oil prices above $100 and the disruption around the Strait of Hormuz. Higher energy costs could increase inflation pressures across energy-importing economies and influence expectations for future interest-rate decisions.

morningSummary.title: 🌍 RadiantWaves Evening News & Update
morningSummary.content: Good evening. The dominant story tonight is the sharp escalation in the US-Iran conflict and its growing impact on global shipping and energy markets. Brent crude has broken above $100 while traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has fallen sharply. In Africa, Dangote is planning a major refinery project in Kenya while Nigerian families continue seeking answers after a mass kidnapping. Europe is dealing with renewed energy-security concerns and the fallout from a major UK air-traffic control failure.

bigQuestion: If the current Middle East conflict continues to disrupt global energy supplies, how much pressure can ordinary households and businesses absorb before the economic impact becomes too severe?
